$comment: Rule catalog — probability. Standard 1. Includes three prohibitions: confusing probability with expected value, fabricating probabilities, and changing methodology in silence.

rules.title: The probability is defined against a resolvable outcome
rules.description: The subject block states the event, the exact condition that counts as the outcome occurring, and who settles it.
rules.rationale: An outcome definition that is merely present is not necessarily precise, but one that is absent is certainly not.
rules.remediation: State the resolution condition in falsifiable terms and name the settling source.
rules.$assuranceNote: A structural check establishes that an outcome definition was written. It cannot establish that the definition is unambiguous, which is the property that actually matters.

rules.title: Every probability lies in the unit interval
rules.description: The predicted probability, the interval bounds, the baseline, the market-implied probability, and every ensemble member probability lie between 0 and 1 inclusive.
rules.rationale: A number outside [0, 1] is not a probability. It is usually a percentage that lost its conversion, and every downstream computation built on it — edge, expected value, aggregation — is wrong in a way that looks numeric rather than conceptual.
rules.remediation: Convert percentages to proportions at the boundary where they enter the record.

rules.title: The methodology that produced the number is named and versioned
rules.description: The record names its methodology and the version of it that ran.
rules.rationale: Two predictions are only comparable if they were made the same way. Without a version, a change of method is invisible even to the people who made it.
rules.remediation: Record the methodology name and a version that changes whenever the method does.
rules.$assuranceNote: The evaluator observes that a name and version were recorded. It cannot observe whether the version was incremented when the method actually changed.

rules.title: A change of prediction methodology is never silent
rules.description: Where successive records share a seriesId, a change in methodology version is accompanied by changedFromPrevious and a note explaining what changed.
rules.rationale: A series of predictions reads as a trend. When the method changes underneath it, movement caused by the change is indistinguishable from movement in the world, and the trend becomes an artefact nobody can see.
rules.remediation: Set changedFromPrevious and write changeNote whenever the methodology version differs from the previous record in the series.
rules.$assuranceNote: Detectable only across records that share a seriesId and are evaluated together. A methodology change between records that carry no seriesId, or that are checked one at a time, is invisible to this rule.

rules.title: A probability is never presented as an expected value
rules.description: The output block carries a probability and nothing monetary. Expected value lives in its own block, requires a stake and a payout, and is recomputed from the probability rather than substituted for it.
rules.rationale: Probability answers how likely an outcome is; expected value answers what a wager on it is worth. They have different units and different decision rules, and a system that lets one stand in for the other will recommend a bet with a high probability and a negative return.
rules.remediation: Keep the probability in output.probability. If a monetary quantity is intended, state stake and payout and put it in expectedValue.

rules.title: A probability is not fabricated
rules.description: A stated probability traces to a named methodology and at least one data source. A number with neither behind it is an invention.
rules.rationale: A fabricated probability is worse than no prediction, because it carries the authority of a number while resting on nothing. Downstream consumers cannot tell the difference by looking.
rules.remediation: Record the methodology and the data sources the probability was derived from, or replace the prediction with an abstention.
rules.$assuranceNote: A structural check establishes that a methodology and sources were CITED. It cannot establish that the number came from them. A probability typed in by hand and attributed to a real model passes this check; only human review, recorded as an attestation, can establish otherwise.
